name: Centro (Market and Ex-Convento)
tagline: The historic heart, market days and all
description: The main square, weekend artisan and food market, and the 16th-century Dominican ex-convento anchor this area. It is the most walkable, amenity-dense part of town, with the highest concentration of cafes, restaurants, and shops, but also the loudest and most crowded, especially on weekends when day-trippers arrive from Mexico City.
cons: Noise from foot traffic and events

name: Barrio de la Santisima
tagline: Quiet cobblestone lanes just off the center
description: A residential barrio a short walk from the main square, known for narrow cobbled streets, colorful facades, and its own small chapel and local festivals. It offers a calmer, more local atmosphere than Centro while staying close enough to walk in for groceries, cafes, or the market.
bestFor: longer stays, people wanting quiet with easy center access

name: Santo Domingo
tagline: Hillside streets with views toward the Tepozteco
description: A neighborhood climbing the lower slopes toward the cliffs, popular with long-term expats and retreat-goers for its views and slightly cooler air. Houses here often have gardens or rooftop terraces looking out at the mountains, though the walk into town involves a noticeable uphill return.
bestFor: long-term renters, remote workers wanting a home office view
pros: Popular with wellness and retreat community
cons: Need a car or taxi at night

name: Amatlan de Quetzalcoatl
tagline: A mystic village outpost outside town
description: A small village about 20 minutes from Tepoztlan center, tied by legend to the birthplace of Quetzalcoatl and known for temazcal ceremonies, healers, and a strong alternative-wellness scene. It is rural and slow-paced, appealing to those seeking deep quiet and nature over convenience.
bestFor: wellness retreats, nature seekers, long solo stays
pros: Close to hiking trails and waterfalls
